chunks: And it is narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) that he said:

The signs of the believer are five: the prayer of fifty [rak'ahs], the visitation of forty [people/occasions], wearing a ring on the right hand, dusting the forehead [with earth during prostration], and reciting 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' aloud.

key_terms.التختّم في اليمين: Wearing a ring on the right hand
key_terms.الجهر بـبسم الله الرحمن الرحيم: Reciting 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' aloud
key_terms.تعفير الجبين: Dusting the forehead [with earth/dirt, emphasizing deep prostration]
key_terms.زيارة الأربعين: The visitation of forty [referring to visiting forty believers or a specific devotional practice]
key_terms.صلاة الخمسين: The prayer of fifty [rak'ahs, likely referring to Dhuhr or a specific devotional prayer]

ai.seo_question: What are the five signs of a believer according to Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) identifies five physical and devotional markers that distinguish a true believer, emphasizing both ritual precision and public declaration of faith. Notably, the 'prayer of fifty' likely refers to the five daily prayers performed with the full count of fifty rak'ahs (including Sunnah), while 'forehead dusting' highlights the humility of sujood, and 'speaking Basmala aloud' underscores the communal aspect of worship. These signs collectively reflect a holistic piety that integrates inner conviction with visible, consistent practice.
